persona: Friendly and chatty; calls her home policy "contents insurance" by mistake and corrects herself if asked. Has two photos, the locksmith's note, the builder's quote and the Police page saying the reference is pending.
initial_message: Hi, I want to make a claim on my contents insurance. Somebody broke in through the front door of my house on Wednesday 23 September - they smashed the glass panel beside the door, snapped the lock and the door is split. I've reported it online, but the event number is still pending with Police.

design.notes: Not yet available: the Police event reference. The fact sheet uses "pending", "not issued yet" and "later", which main matches for a pending Police report.

triage.rationale: The Police event reference is pending (an unavailable notice; Police will email it later), so the Police report a burglary needs is not available yet (evidence_outstanding). The builder's quote totals NZD 6,072.00 including GST, over NZD 5,000 (amount_over_threshold_or_unknown). The claimant names contents insurance, but nothing was taken and the damage is to the building, so the claim belongs in home (G3); that is a wording slip, not a dispute of terms. The door is secured, the home habitable, nobody is hurt and no other party is involved. Main's theft branch also lists proof of ownership; nothing was taken, so the pack treats the photo, the repair quote and the Police report as the required materials. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt, proof of purchase or proof of ownership in the pack; nothing was taken

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 April 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2024-04-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
